title: The pulse and downstrokes
summary: Strum down on every beat and switch between E minor and A minor without losing the pulse.

steps.title: Meet E minor
steps.text: Two fingers, and all six strings ring. Watch where each finger goes, then copy the shape.

steps.title: Meet A minor
steps.text: Am looks like Em moved down one string, plus your index finger. Skip the thickest string.

steps.title: Strum on the beat
steps.text: One downstroke on each click: 1, 2, 3, 4. Your hand still comes back up between beats, it just misses the strings.

steps.title: Play along
steps.text: Two bars of Em, two bars of Am. If a change is late, keep strumming anyway: the pulse matters more than a perfect chord.

steps.title: Check yourself
steps.goal: 4 bars at 70 bpm without losing the pulse

title: Down-up eighth notes
summary: Add upstrokes between the beats for a steady down-up motion.

steps.title: Down on the number, up on the "and"
steps.text: Count "1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and". Down on the numbers, up on every "and". Upstrokes are lighter: mostly the thin strings.

steps.title: Play along
steps.text: Keep your wrist loose and the motion even, like shaking water off your hand.

title: The folk pattern
summary: Learn ↓ ↓↑ ↑↓↑, the pattern behind countless acoustic pop songs.

steps.title: Meet G major
steps.text: Three fingers spread across the neck. All six strings ring.

steps.title: Meet D major
steps.text: A small triangle on the thin strings. Start your strum on the 4th string.
Your hand never stops: down-up on every beat. On the "and" of 1 and on beat 3 it moves without touching the strings.

steps.title: Play along
steps.text: Say it out loud: "down, down-up, up-down-up". Start slow; speed comes on its own.

steps.title: Check yourself
steps.goal: 8 bars of the folk pattern without stopping

title: F with a partial barre
summary: Get the F chord to ring on four strings, with an easy version to start.

steps.title: The easy F first
steps.text: Fmaj7 sounds close to F and needs no barre. Use it in songs while the real F gets stronger.

steps.title: F with a small barre
steps.text: Lay your index finger flat across the two thinnest strings at fret 1. Roll it slightly onto its bony side so both strings ring.

steps.title: C → F → C → G
steps.text: From C, your ring and middle fingers move up one string each, and your index flattens. Strum only the 4 thin strings on F.

steps.title: Check yourself
steps.goal: F rings on all 4 strings in time, twice through
